name: first_hour_range_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: NIFTY's first trading hour (09:15-10:15) absorbs overnight information, FII pre-positioning, and opening auction imbalances, forming a well-anchored high-low range. Many institutional TWAP algorithms and bracket-order participants set stop-losses just outside this range. When NIFTY closes above the first-hour high (or below the low) with elevated volume post-10:15, it triggers a cascade of stop-loss orders and directional VWAP algorithms that had been range-bound, creating a 20-35 spot point momentum burst in the first 30-90 seconds. We enter at the second consecutive close above/below the range level — this filters 5-second spikes — and ride the initial cascade momentum rather than the full multi-hour continuation.

indicators.name: fhr_high
indicators.purpose: Fixed time window: 09:15-10:15 = 60 min = 720 bars at 5s. NOT scaled — the first hour range is the same 60-minute window regardless of bar size. This is the supply ceiling from which stop-loss cascades originate. Frozen after 10:15 and forward-filled for the rest of the session.

indicators.name: fhr_low
indicators.purpose: Fixed time window, same logic as fhr_high. Defines the demand floor where resting buy stops accumulate during the first hour.

indicators.name: fhr_width_pct
indicators.purpose: Quality filter: range too tight (<0.30%) means any breakout is noise; range too wide (>1.50%) indicates a gap-heavy day where the range structure is unreliable as an anchor. The filter selects structurally clean first-hour ranges.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumulative(typical_price * volume) / cumulative(volume), reset per session_date
indicators.purpose: Cumulative VWAP — no lookback scaling needed. Used as directional confirmation: breakout above FHR high is only traded if price is also above VWAP (institutional benchmark), ensuring we're not buying into VWAP resistance.

indicators.name: vol_ratio_60
indicators.purpose: 60 bars = 5-minute rolling volume average. Matches the original's 20-bar 1-min window (both 5 minutes of context). Detects elevated volume on the breakout bar, which distinguishes genuine institutional stop-cascade breakouts from low-participation drifts.

conditions: close[i] > fhr_high AND close[i-1] > fhr_high (2-bar persistence, same-day FHR)
buy_ce.confirmation: Two consecutive 5-second closes above fhr_high — filters single-bar spikes without adding lag (10 seconds total)

conditions: close[i] < fhr_low AND close[i-1] < fhr_low (2-bar persistence, same-day FHR)

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. A genuine FHR breakout on NIFTY should not retrace 8+ spot points in the first 90 seconds — if it does, the stop-cascade thesis has failed and the market is likely to re-enter the range. Calibrated to NIFTY's typical 30s move of 2-5 option pts: a 4-pt stop allows 1 full typical 30s adverse move before stopping out.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points. FHR breakout cascades on NIFTY typically produce 20-35 spot point bursts in the first 60-90 seconds; 14 spot points captures roughly 50% of the expected initial move. At 1:1.75 R:R (4 stop : 7 target), the strategy is profitable at 37% win rate before costs.

filters.vix_filter: vix between 12 and 25 — below 12 suggests dead-market with no follow-through; above 25 is event-driven with unpredictable cascades
filters.time_filter: entry only between 10:15 IST and 14:30 IST — requires first-hour to be complete, avoids late-day illiquidity
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar vol_ratio >= 1.30 vs 5-min rolling average
filters.trend_filter: VWAP confirmation — trade long breakouts only above VWAP, short breakouts only below VWAP
filters.spread_filter: not applicable (limit order execution at 5s close)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — as algorithmic participation grows, stop clusters just outside FHR may become well-known and hunted, reducing the cascade reliability

adaptation_notes: Major changes from original: (1) HOLD TIME compressed from 60-240 min to 15-90 seconds — we capture only the initial stop-cascade momentum burst, not the multi-hour continuation. (2) FHR fixed window (09:15-10:15 = 720 5s bars) unchanged — same 60-minute anchor. (3) Volume filter adapted from 20-bar 1-min rolling avg to 60-bar 5s rolling avg (both equal 5 minutes of context). (4) Trailing stop removed — too complex for 5s holds. (5) Target changed from 1x range width (which would be 50-100+ option points — far too large) to a fixed 7 option points calibrated to the initial momentum burst magnitude. (6) Entry confirmation reduced from 2 1-min bars (2 minutes) to 2 5-second bars (10 seconds) — sufficient to filter spikes at this frequency.
weaknesses: Low frequency: 0-2 valid FHR breakouts per day on NIFTY; many days have no breakout or breakout occurs after 14:30 cutoff
On expiry days, the first-hour range is often gapped or erratic, making FHR levels unreliable anchors
The 2-bar confirmation (10 seconds) means we enter after the first bar above the level, potentially missing faster spikes
VIX filter 12-25 may exclude high-volatility days where breakouts are actually strongest
